title: Apache HTTP Server Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Apache HTTP Server lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: An HTTP server sends responses
entries.summary: Apache HTTP Server accepts web requests and sends responses. For a static site, the response body often comes straight from a file.

example.code:
Request: GET /club.html
Response status: 200 if the file is served
Response body: the HTML file

notes: Apache HTTP Server is not the same project as every other tool with Apache in its name.

entries.name: Listen on a practice port
entries.summary: Listen selects the address and port where Apache accepts connections. Bind a local experiment to loopback.
notes: Do not bind a learning server to every network interface without understanding the exposure.

entries.name: Virtual hosts choose a site
entries.summary: A virtual host groups configuration for a site. ServerName identifies the intended host name.
notes: The first matching virtual host can affect requests with unexpected hostnames; review the whole configuration.

entries.name: Directory access is explicit
entries.summary: A Directory block applies settings to a filesystem directory. Access rules should expose only intended public files.
notes: Never grant public access to an entire home directory just to serve one page.

entries.name: Choose the first page
entries.summary: DirectoryIndex lists candidate files for a directory request. The first existing suitable file can be used.
notes: A missing index file is not a reason to expose private directory contents.

entries.name: Understand URL and file paths
entries.summary: A URL path and a filesystem path are different. DocumentRoot usually provides the base used to map a URL path to a file.
notes: Do not let a user choose an arbitrary filesystem path.

entries.name: MIME types describe files
entries.summary: A MIME type tells the browser what kind of response it is receiving. Apache uses configured mappings and modules for common file types.

example.code:
CSS: text/css
JSON: application/json
HTML: text/html

notes: A 200 response containing the wrong file type can still break the page.

entries.name: Modules add features
entries.summary: Apache modules add features such as headers, rewriting or TLS. A directive may require its matching module to be loaded.
notes: Do not assume every Apache installation loads the same modules.

entries.name: Read htaccess limits
entries.summary: An .htaccess file can apply permitted directory settings when the server allows overrides. It is not always enabled or needed.

example.code:
Server-level choice: AllowOverride None
Result: .htaccess overrides are not used for that directory

notes: Do not enable every override merely to make an unfamiliar snippet work.

entries.name: Custom error documents
entries.summary: ErrorDocument can point to a local page that explains a status such as not found.
notes: Do not make a missing script return the home page with a success status.

entries.name: Logs explain requests and problems
entries.summary: Apache access logs record request information. Error logs help diagnose server failures or configuration problems.

example.code:
Access log question: which URL was requested?
Error log question: why could the server not read the file?

notes: Do not publish logs as static website files.

entries.name: Check before changing a server
entries.summary: Validate the configuration before an approved reload, then test real routes and assets. A syntax check does not prove the whole website works.
notes: Do not reload or stop an organisation's server as a learning experiment.
